test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What was India’s unemployment rate in May 2025, as per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** data indicates that the **unemployment rate** in India for the period of **May 2025** stood at **5.6%**.
 
• The **unemployment rate (UR)** is calculated as the percentage of persons unemployed among the total persons in the **labour force**.
 
• The **PLFS** is an initiative by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, which functions under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** of the **Government of India**.
 
• The primary objective of the **PLFS** is to estimate the key employment and unemployment indicators such as the **Worker Population Ratio (WPR)**, **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)**, and **Unemployment Rate (UR)** in a short time interval of three months for **urban areas** only in the **Current Weekly Status (CWS)**.
 
• The survey was launched in **April 2017** to ensure the availability of more frequent labour force data to help in **evidence-based policy making**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)**:
 
 
• This refers to the percentage of the population that is either working or actively seeking work. It includes both the **employed** and the **unemployed** seeking employment.
 
 
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR)**:
 
 
• It is defined as the percentage of **employed persons** in the total population. This metric helps in understanding the proportion of the population that is actively contributing to the **production of goods and services** in the **economy**.
 
 
 
• **Activity Status Definitions**:
 
 
• **Usual Status**: The activity status is determined based on the reference period of the last **365 days** preceding the date of the survey.
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS)**: The activity status is determined based on a reference period of the last **7 days** preceding the date of the survey.
 
 
 
• **Significance of PLFS**:
 
 
• Before the **PLFS**, the **NSSO** used to conduct **quinquennial (every five years)** surveys on employment. The shift to **PLFS** allows the **Government** to track the **employment market** dynamics with much higher frequency, especially in **urban centers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **unemployment rate** of **5.6%** reflects the status of individuals who were available for work but could not find even **one hour** of work during the reference week.
 
• **MoSPI** releases quarterly bulletins that provide estimates for **urban areas** and annual reports that cover both **rural and urban** sectors of **India**.
 
• Data from the **PLFS** is often compared with other reports like those from the **Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE)**, though the methodologies and definitions used by the **NSSO** are considered the official benchmarks for **Government** planning.
 
• Factors influencing these rates include **economic growth**, **educational attainment**, **skill development** initiatives, and **seasonal variations** in sectors like **agriculture** and **construction**.
